summary: The article accurately reports on recent changes to India's foreign exchange rules, specifically regarding inventory-based e-commerce for exporting Indian-made goods. The dates, rule numbers, and implications are correctly stated.

claims.claim: The Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic Affairs, issued a notification on September 2, 2026, introducing these changes through the Foreign Exchange Management (Non-debt Instruments) (Fourth Amendment) Rules, 2026.
claims.note: The Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic Affairs, issued a notification on September 2, 2026, introducing the Foreign Exchange Management (Non-debt Instruments) (Fourth Amendment) Rules, 2026.

claims.claim: The government has added a new entry (15.2.5) to Schedule I of the Foreign Exchange Management (Non-debt Instruments) Rules, 2019.
claims.note: The key change has been introduced in Schedule I of the Foreign Exchange Management (Non-debt Instruments) Rules, 2019 by adding a new entry, 15.2.5.

claims.claim: This new entry specifically states that an e-commerce entity can now engage in an inventory-based model *exclusively for exporting goods or products manufactured or produced in India*.
claims.note: Under the new provision, an e-commerce entity can engage in an inventory-based model of e-commerce exclusively for exporting goods or products manufactured or produced in India.

claims.claim: The amendment clarifies that previous restrictions on B2C transactions and inventory-based e-commerce models (found in older rules like 15.2.1 to 15.2.4) will *not* apply when Indian-made goods are being exported through e-commerce under this new provision.
claims.note: The amendment also provides an important relaxation for e-commerce exports. The restrictions relating to Business-to-Consumer (B2C) transactions and inventory-based e-commerce models mentioned under serial numbers 15.2.1 to 15.2.4 will not apply when Indian-made goods are exported through e-commerce under the newly inserted provision.

claims.claim: Businesses still need to follow other important rules. These include the Foreign Trade Policy 2023, the Handbook of Procedures (HBP), and the Foreign Exchange Management (Export of Goods & Services) Regulations, 2015.
claims.note: Such exports must comply with the provisions of the Foreign Trade Policy 2023, the Handbook of Procedures (HBP) and the Foreign Exchange Management (Export of Goods & Services) Regulations, 2015.

article_title: Your Local Products Can Now Reach the World Easier: New Export Rules for Online Sellers
